subject: Asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters

messages.author: 13deaaee5806ffce
messages.subject: Asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to obtain the full asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters. For example, the following example is taken from http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html

lavaan provides standard errors on ab and total. Is it possible to obtain the asymptotic covariance matrix? Thanks.
set.seed(1234)
X <- rnorm(100)
M <- 0.5*X + rnorm(100)
Y <- 0.7*M + rnorm(100)
Data <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y, M = M)
model <- ' # direct effect
             Y ~ c*X
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X
             Y ~ b*M
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)'
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)
summary(fit)
Regards,
Mike

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters
parts:
On 04/04/2014 06:45 AM, Mike Cheung wrote:
> Dear Oscar,
>
> Thanks for your reply. It is not in this case. Since "ab" and "total"
> are not parameters in the model, vcov() does not work. I can obtain it
> by using the delta method. Since lavaan has already implemented it the
> delta method to obtain the SEs, I wonder whether I can get the full matrix.

I am afraid not (yet).

You can do it manually, using some internal functions, like this:

set.seed(1234)
X <- rnorm(100)
M <- 0.5*X + rnorm(100)
Y <- 0.7*M + rnorm(100)
Data <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y, M = M)
model <- ' # direct effect
Y ~ c*X
# mediator
M ~ a*X
Y ~ b*M
# indirect effect (a*b)
ab := a*b
# total effect
total := c + (a*b)'
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)

# first get ordinary vcov
VCOV <- vcov(fit)

# extract free parameters
x <- fit@Fit@x

# compute jacobian for 'defined parameters'
JAC <- lavaan:::lavJacobianD(func = fit@Mod...@def.function, x = x)

# vcov for defined parameters, using delta method
VCOV.def <- JAC %*% VCOV %*% t(JAC)

If you need the 'full' vcov, just combine VCOV and VCOV.def in a block
diagonal matrix:

lavaan:::bdiag(VCOV, VCOV.def)

But lavaan should return this out of the box. I will add this to my TODO
list.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters
parts:
Dear Yves,

I am facing the exact same Problem as Mike. Unfortunately, vcov(), as well as coef(), still dont consider the newly defined parameters. In your aforementioned manual solution, the vcov() of the defined parameters is generated straightforwardly. However, using this approach, we only get the 2 (out of 3) parts of the FULL asymptotic variance covariance matrix of all parameters. That is, we get the vcov of model parameters, that of newly defined parameters, but I need the covariances between the model parameters and the newly defined parameters. Could you tell me how to obtain these?

Also, consider this a request to implement the full vcov() in future versions of lavaan. Since this is standard in MPlus Tech 3, I have to fall back to that for now (and I really don't want to ;)).

Sincerely
Julian

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Asymptotic covariance matrix of functions of parameters
parts:
In lavaan dev 0.6-4.1337 (or higher), lavInspect(fit, "vcov.def.joint")
will return the *joint* variance matrix of both the free parameters and
the defined parameters.

To follow up on the example, this is how it is done:

set.seed(1234)
X <- rnorm(100)
M <- 0.5*X + rnorm(100)
Y <- 0.7*M + rnorm(100)
Data <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y, M = M)
model <- ' # direct effect
Y ~ c*X
# mediator
M ~ a*X
Y ~ b*M
# indirect effect (a*b)
ab := a*b
# total effect
total := c + (a*b)'
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)

# first get ordinary vcov
VCOV <- vcov(fit)

# extract free parameters
x <- coef(fit)
# compute jacobian for 'defined parameters'

JAC <- numDeriv:::jacobian(func = fit@Mod...@def.function, x = x)

# add identity matrix for free parameters
JAC2 <- rbind(diag(nrow = ncol(JAC)), JAC)
VCOV.joint <- JAC2 %*% VCOV %*% t(JAC2)

Yves.
